question: Clomiphene citrate induces ovulation primarily by which mechanism, and what is its most significant clinical risk?

answers.text: Directly stimulating FSH release from the pituitary; hyperprolactinaemia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clomiphene does not directly stimulate FSH. It works indirectly through oestrogen receptor blockade at the hypothalamus.

answers.text: Blocking oestrogen receptors in the hypothalamus → removing negative feedback → increased GnRH/FSH/LH; multiple gestation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! By blocking hypothalamic oestrogen receptors, clomiphene prevents negative feedback → pulsatile GnRH → FSH surge → follicular development. Multiple gestation (twins ~8–10%) is the most significant risk.

answers.text: Stimulating GnRH receptors continuously to downregulate the pituitary; ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Continuous GnRH stimulation (as with GnRH agonists) causes pituitary desensitisation, the opposite of the clomiphene effect. Severe OHSS is more associated with gonadotrophins.

answers.text: Inhibiting aromatase to reduce oestrogen levels; premature menopause

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Aromatase inhibition describes letrozole (alternative ovulation inducer in PCOS). Clomiphene is an oestrogen receptor modulator, not an aromatase inhibitor.

overallFeedback.feedback: Clomiphene blocks hypothalamic ER → removes negative feedback → GnRH pulse increase → FSH/LH rise → folliculogenesis. Multiple pregnancy rate ~8–10% is the main risk to counsel about.
Excellent! Clomiphene's anti-oestrogenic action at the hypothalamus is the key to understanding its mechanism — and why multiple follicles sometimes develop.
